mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over the preceding three months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% per month for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when inflation expectations rise sharply as measured by breakeven proxies (not available here, but would be tested if added).

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% coincident with a flattening industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 YoY change < -2% AND INDPRO monthly change < 0 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when the decline is accompanied by a simultaneous surge in labor market indicators (PAYEMS).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 5% for two consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered months, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth (not observable here, but would be tested if INDPRO were included in a regime filter).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of more than 0.5% for three consecutive months signals a contraction in the manufacturing supply base, which raises input costs and reduces corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when accompanied by a simultaneous surge in demand proxies (e.g., HOUST or GDPC1).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp one-month spike in the federal funds rate to above 4.5% without a concurrent rise in inflation expectations (not observable here, but as a base case) signals front-loaded tightening, which immediately reduces equity valuations and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS jumps > 0.75% in one month to > 4.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered events, or the mechanism fails when accompanied by a simultaneous surge in inflation proxies (e.g., CPIAUCSL).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both housing starts (HOUST) and personal savings (RSAFS) above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a rebalancing toward future consumption, which boosts optimism and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-mo MA AND RSAFS > 12-mo MA simultaneously
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rising unemployment (UNRATE).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly increase in payroll employment (PAYEMS) of more than 0.5% for four consecutive months signals robust labor market expansion, which boosts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS monthly change > 0.5% for 4 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when wage growth (not observable here) is stagnant.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) coupled with a simultaneous rise in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests a shift from consumption to investment-led growth, which can support equity valuations and produce positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly change < -0.2% AND INDPRO monthly change > 0.3% for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: transition from consumption- to investment-led growth
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when the investment boom is not accompanied by stable monetary policy (e.g., FEDFUNDS volatility).
